_comment: The live seven-lesson Grade 1 build, described for ../../lesson-app-tools. The five tools in ../ built this directory and still work; this config exists so the SHARED tools (wire-progress.py, check-lessons.py) can be pointed at it without another hardcoded path. Order here IS the unit number.
subject: mathematics
_extraPages: lesson-search.json is the lesson-content search index, derived from these pages by ../../lesson-app-tools/build-lesson-search.py and fetched by the hub and every lesson page. It is listed here because extraPages is what deploy.mjs uploads beside the lessons; without it the field would ship and answer nothing.

lessons.title: Counting to Twenty
lessons.atHome: Gather up to 20 small things, such as beans or bottle tops. Ask your child to guess how many, then count them by touching each one once. Then put them in pairs: if every one has a partner the number is even, and if one is left alone it is odd.

lessons.title: Adding and Taking Away
lessons.atHome: Put 10 beans on the table and hide some under a cup. Ask how many are hidden: if 6 are showing, 4 are hidden, because 6 and 4 make 10. For doubles, put the same number in each hand and ask how many there are altogether.

lessons.title: Halves and Wholes
lessons.atHome: At snack time, cut a piece of fruit or bread into two parts and ask whether they are the same size: only two equal parts are halves. Then share 6 beans fairly between two people, so each person has half.

lessons.title: What Comes Next
lessons.atHome: Make a pattern with things to hand, such as spoon, cup, spoon, cup, and ask what comes next. Then ask your child to make a pattern for you to carry on, and to point to the part that repeats.

lessons.title: Shapes and Sizes
lessons.atHome: Go on a shape hunt at home: find something round, something with four straight sides, and something shaped like a box. Then compare two objects and ask which is longer, which is heavier, and which holds more water.

lessons.title: Days, Months and Clocks
lessons.atHome: Each morning, say the day of the week together and ask what day comes next. Look at a clock with hands, or draw one, and ask where the short hand and the long hand point at an o'clock time and at half past.

lessons.title: Asking and Sorting
lessons.atHome: Ask everyone at home one question, such as their favourite fruit, and record the answers together as a list or with tally marks. Then sort some clothes or toys into two groups, such as red and not red, and count each group.
